android.desc:
Liar's dice for the places the internet can't reach — a row on a flight, a subway car, a campsite, a cabin. Phones find each other over Bluetooth and the whole game runs at the table.

Joining a table is free. Hosting tables is a one-time purchase. One unlocked host per table is all a whole game needs.

Buy the unlock before you fly: purchasing needs a connection, but once unlocked, hosting works fully offline.

HOW IT WORKS
• One player hosts a table; up to five more join from the nearby-tables list. No hotspot, no pairing screens, no internet, just Bluetooth.
• Closed tables are protected by a code the host shares. Open tables let anyone nearby ask to join, and the host lets each player in.
• Classic liar's dice: bid on the whole table's dice, or call the bluff. Ones are wild (house rule to turn them off).
• Peek at your roll under the cup; hold to call LIAR.
• Table chat
• Optional alert when someone nearby opens a table to all (off by default).

quotes.text:
I remember being able to play poker and trivia with random strangers on cross country flights on the IFE screens. For some reason, they took that away, so I decided to make some myself.
The first two games are here: Poker - 
* iOS: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/airplane-mode-poker/id6791247916
* Android: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=de.testco.airplanemode.poker

Liar's Dice -
* Android: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=de.testco.airplanemode.liarsdice
* [iOS still in review]

BLE was the choice to have it work cross-platform and support multiple players. There is no Internet access and there is no analytics or app tracking. The game literally doesn't ask for the permissions to access the Internet.

It costs $2.99 as a one time unlock to host and $0 to join a game.

Thoughts on other games?
